credentials.description: Notch Pay public key, sent as is in Authorization; a key containing test_ works in sandbox (same host for test and live)
Notch Pay private key, sent as is in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: Send money to a beneficiary via MTN MoMo or Orange Money using Notch Pay.

amount.description: Amount to transfer. Integer for XAF (no decimals).

beneficiary.description: ID of an existing beneficiary. Either beneficiary or recipient+channel is required.

recipient.description: Phone number or account number of the recipient. Used with channel when no saved beneficiary.

channel.description: Payment channel slug (e.g. "cm.mtn", "cm.orange"). Required when using recipient instead of beneficiary.

reference.description: Optional unique reference you assign to this transfer for reconciliation. Auto-generated if omitted; reusing a reference returns a 422 conflict.
Transfer reference. Store this to call verify_transfer later.

gotchas: Transfers are not immediately settled — the initial status is "pending". Always call verify_transfer (GET /transfers/{reference}) to confirm completion before recording the disbursement as successful.
Either beneficiary (saved beneficiary ID) or the recipient+channel pair is required. Providing neither returns a 422 error.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
Your server's IP address must be whitelisted in the Notch Pay dashboard before API transfers will be accepted. Requests from non-whitelisted IPs are rejected regardless of valid API credentials.

Authorization takes your public key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix, and X-Grant your private key (Notch Pay's Authentication page: `-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`).

The currency must match the channel's country: XAF for cm.* channels (Cameroon), XOF for ci.*/sn.* (Côte d'Ivoire/Senegal), KES for ke.* (Kenya), UGX for ug.* (Uganda), GHS for gh.* (Ghana). A mismatch returns 422.

Notch Pay documents no idempotency header; duplicates are prevented by the transfer reference: "Use unique, idempotent references for each transfer to prevent duplicate transfers and simplify reconciliation." (Notch Pay API reference, Transfers, Best Practices). Set `reference` yourself so a retry carries the same value.
open_questions: What does Notch Pay return when a transfer is retried with a reference already used? Its docs (https://developer.notchpay.co/api-reference/transfers.md) only ask for "unique, idempotent references"; the 422 conflict in this spec's `reference` description is not found there (its 422 examples are insufficient balance, unknown beneficiary and invalid channel).
